name: American Water Works
headline: The largest US water utility, with exclusive service areas in fourteen states and a regulator-set return.
what_short: Regulated water and wastewater utility, 14 states
what_it_does: American Water Works supplies drinking water and treats wastewater in fourteen US states. Each service area is an exclusive franchise, because no one can lay a second set of pipes, and state regulators set the prices it may charge. No single state is more than a quarter of revenue.
why_it_passed: No competitor can build a second pipe network, and the service certificate is exclusive, so its customers cannot go elsewhere.
Its operating margin averaged 34.3% over ten years, close to the 35.7% of rival Essential Utilities and well above California Water's 16.8%.
More states are moving toward rules that let utilities recover costs sooner, such as future test years (Missouri from July 2026) and infrastructure surcharges in nine states.
The accounts are clean and no doubts about management's honesty were found.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what a utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $141.10 a share a buyer would earn about 3.6% to 5.0% a year, less than the 5.30% on a 30-year US Treasury bond, and the analysis's value range is only $94.91 to $98.84.
watch: Its prices and returns are political: regulators decide how much of its costs it may recover.
It is merging with Essential Utilities (stock for stock, bringing a gas utility), with an $835 million termination fee payable by American Water in some circumstances.
Total debt is about $16 billion, and spending on pipes and plants is large, continuous and largely compulsory.
